# public-value

> A Rust crate of public value models, structs, and calculations for software engineers building
> for governmental and social sector organizations: value for money, cost-benefit and
> cost-effectiveness analysis, social return on investment, the Human Development Index, DORA
> metrics translated into public-value terms, and 59 other formulas and frameworks. Each of the 64
> core items is ported from one topic in the `public-value-metrics` book
> (https://github.com/public-value-metrics/public-value-metrics), with a doctest reproducing that
> topic's worked example. A further 11 items (QALYs, DALYs, the Gini coefficient, the
> Inequality-adjusted HDI, Net Promoter Score) are independently researched extensions completing
> connections the source topics reference but don't implement — see spec/topics.md's "Extensions"
> section.

Money, Ratio, and Percentage are typed newtypes, not plain `f64` — `Money` is backed by
`rusty_money::Money` for exact decimal arithmetic, with every value tagged to a single fixed
internal working currency (`USD`) so amounts built anywhere in the crate can always be combined.
Every public function is `#[must_use]` and documented; `#![deny(missing_docs)]` and
`#![deny(clippy::pedantic)]` are enforced crate-wide.

## Docs

- [README](README.md): module list, quick-start example, testing instructions.
- [Getting started tutorial](docs/tutorials/getting-started.md): a worked business case spanning
  three modules.
- [Porting a new topic tutorial](docs/tutorials/porting-a-new-topic.md): the process for adding a
  topic, for maintainers or contributors.
- [Architecture spec](spec/architecture.md): the four modelling shapes, shared newtypes, naming and
  lint conventions — the single source of truth for how this crate is built.
- [Topic mapping spec](spec/topics.md): all 64 source topics mapped to their Rust module and
  primary type/function.

## Modules

- [`units`](src/units.rs): the shared `Money`/`Ratio`/`Percentage` newtypes every other module uses.
- [`foundations`](src/foundations.rs): public value foundations (the strategic triangle, value for
  money, opportunity cost, the social discount rate, distributional weighting, deadweight,
  displacement, counterfactual analysis).
- [`economic_appraisal`](src/economic_appraisal.rs): the Green Book five-case model, social
  cost-benefit analysis, cost-effectiveness analysis, multi-criteria decision analysis, wellbeing
  valuation, stated/revealed preference valuation, shadow pricing.
- [`impact_measurement`](src/impact_measurement.rs): social return on investment, theory of change,
  logic models, outcomes vs outputs, the Social Value Act, unit cost databases, impact evaluation
  methods.
- [`performance_metrics`](src/performance_metrics.rs): public sector KPIs, the public value
  scorecard, outcomes-based accountability, payment by results, public service productivity,
  citizen satisfaction, service standards, trust and legitimacy metrics.
- [`philanthropy_metrics`](src/philanthropy_metrics.rs): cost per outcome, cost per beneficiary,
  blended value, effective-altruism-style cost-effectiveness, charity overhead ratio, donor ROI,
  grant outcomes reporting, volunteer time value.
- [`digital_government`](src/digital_government.rs): the digital service standard, cost per
  transaction, channel shift savings, digital inclusion, government as a platform, open data value,
  cybersecurity value, AI in government value.
- [`societal_indicators`](src/societal_indicators.rs): GDP alternatives, the Human Development
  Index, the Multidimensional Poverty Index, wellbeing-adjusted life years, the Index of Multiple
  Deprivation, social capital metrics, natural capital accounting, intergenerational equity.
- [`delivery_connection`](src/delivery_connection.rs): cost of delay, DORA metrics for public
  value, flow metrics, technical debt as public value erosion, total cost of ownership, build vs
  buy, benefits realization, AI productivity in the public sector.

## Optional

- [`llms.json`](llms.json): the same index as structured JSON, for programmatic consumption.
- [`Cargo.toml`](Cargo.toml): dependencies, lint configuration, package metadata.
